adjudication_label: batch_5:Comparative thermal response of W-based HEAs to binary standards
canonical_question: How does the 1050 K annealing result compare to the behavior of pure tungsten or standard W-Ta binary alloys under the same thermal conditions?

question_variants.question: How does the 1050 K annealing result compare to the behavior of pure tungsten or standard W-Ta binary alloys under the same thermal conditions?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided evidence describes the behavior of the W-Ta-Cr-V HEA at 1050 K but contains no comparative data or discussion regarding pure tungsten or standard W-Ta binary alloys under the same conditions.

answers.answer: The evidence confirms that the W-Ta-Cr-V HEA sample was annealed at 1050 K and that compositional layering and segregation to grain boundaries were observed, similar to the as-deposited state. However, the text provides no data, observations, or comparisons for pure tungsten or W-Ta binary alloys under these conditions.
answers.measurement_outcome: Clear compositional layering visible; segregation similar to as-deposited.
answers.mechanism: Heating does not homogenously distribute compositional clustering.
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparative data for pure W or W-Ta alloys available in the text.
evidence_spans: We also checked the nanoscale distribution of elements with APT analysis for an annealed sample at 1050 K (see fig. S3).
Clear compositional layering is visible in both the ion maps and the 2D compositional maps.
The segregation of elements to grain boundaries was also observed to be similar to as-deposited films.
